hints: Notice that first ionisation energy normally rises across Period 3, so focus on where the pattern dips instead of rising.
Recall the two famous dips in Period 3 are at aluminium (lower than magnesium) and at sulfur (lower than phosphorus) due to sub-shell effects.
Now use the oxide clue to decide between those two, by remembering which Period 3 oxides dissolve and react to make acids or alkalis and which are insoluble.
walkthrough:
**List what Period 3 gives us**

Think of the row from left to right: $\text{Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S, Cl, Ar}$. We need an element T whose first ionisation energy is a drop from the element before it.

First ionisation energy means:
$$\text{X(g)} \rightarrow \text{X}^{+}\text{(g)} + \text{e}^{-}$$

**Find where ionisation energy drops**

Across a period, increasing proton number normally pulls electrons tighter, so ionisation energy rises. But there are two well known dips in Period 3.

Mg ($\text{3s}^{2}$) to Al ($\text{3s}^{2}\text{3p}^{1}$) is a drop because the $\text{3p}$ electron is further out and shielded. P ($\text{3p}^{3}$) to S ($\text{3p}^{4}$) is a drop because the paired electrons in S repel each other. So T must be either $\text{Al}$ or $\text{S}$.

**Use the oxide with water test**

Now check oxides. Sodium oxide is basic and reacts: $\text{Na}_{2}\text{O} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}$. Sulfur oxides are acidic and react: $\text{SO}_{2} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{3}$.

Aluminium oxide, $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$, is insoluble and does not react with water. That matches both clues perfectly, so T is aluminium.

options.A: Aluminium fits both clues. Its first ionisation energy is lower than magnesium because its outer electron is in 3p rather than 3s, and its oxide $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$ is insoluble and unreactive with water.
options.B: Silicon is tempting because $\text{SiO}_{2}$ also does not react with water, but its first ionisation energy is higher than aluminium (the element before it), not lower, so it fails the first clue.
options.C: Sodium oxide $\text{Na}_{2}\text{O}$ reacts vigorously with water to form $\text{NaOH}$, and sodium has no element before it in Period 3 to compare ionisation energy with in this way, so it fails both clues.
options.D: Sulfur does show a dip in ionisation energy compared to phosphorus due to spin-pair repulsion, but its oxides $\text{SO}_{2}$ and $\text{SO}_{3}$ dissolve and react with water to form acids, so it fails the oxide clue.
